title: Assess the influence of the environment on sustainable livestock production

lessons.title: The environment and our animals
lessons.html:
What is the environment?

The environment is everything around the animals: the weather, the veld and grass, the water, the soil, the shelter and other animals. The environment affects how well animals grow, breed and stay healthy.

Weather

  • Heat: in hot weather animals pant, look for shade and eat less. Chickens and pigs suffer quickly in heat. Give shade and plenty of clean water.
  • Cold and rain: young animals such as lambs and calves can die of cold, especially when wet and windy. Give shelter.
  • Drought: there is little grass and water. Animals lose weight.

Grass and veld

Cattle, sheep and goats eat veld grass and bushes. In summer the grass is green and good. In winter, in most of South Africa, the grass is dry and has less food value. Animals may need a lick or extra feed in winter. Ask your supervisor what the farm uses.

Water

Animals need clean water every day. A cow drinks a lot more on a hot day. Dirty troughs, broken pipes or a dry dam can make animals ill or thirsty very fast. Check troughs every day.

Different animals, different places

Some breeds handle heat, ticks and poor veld well, such as Nguni cattle and indigenous goats. Other breeds need better feed and care. Farmers choose animals that fit their area.

Look and report

Each day look at the animals, the water, the grass and the shelter. If something is wrong, tell your supervisor. For example: the trough in camp 4 is empty, or the calves are wet and cold after the storm.

lessons.title: How animals can harm the environment
lessons.html:
Looking after the land

Animals need the environment, but they can also damage it. If we damage the veld and water, there will be less food for animals next year.

Overgrazing

Overgrazing happens when too many animals eat in one camp for too long. The good grass dies. Bare soil is left. Weeds and bushes grow. When it rains, the water runs off and takes the soil with it. This is called erosion. Gullies (dongas) form.

Signs of overgrazing

  • Very short grass and bare patches
  • Paths and gullies where water runs
  • Few good grass types, many weeds
  • Thin animals

Trampling

Where animals walk and stand a lot, like around water points, gates and kraals, the soil becomes hard and bare. Move water troughs and lick blocks from time to time if your supervisor agrees.

Water pollution

Manure and urine near rivers and dams make the water dirty. Animals standing in a river damage the banks. Keep kraals and manure heaps away from water. Use troughs instead of letting animals drink in the river where possible.

Dip and medicine waste

Old dip and empty medicine containers can poison water, fish and wild animals. Never throw dip into a river or empty bottles in the veld. Follow the farm's rules for waste.

Example

On one farm, sheep stayed in the same camp next to the river all winter. By spring the grass was gone, the river bank was broken and the water was muddy. When the farm started moving the sheep through all the camps, the grass grew back.

lessons.title: Farming in a sustainable way
lessons.html:
Using the land so it lasts

Sustainable means we can keep farming for many years without destroying the land, water and animals. The law also asks farmers to look after soil and veld; the Conservation of Agricultural Resources Act 43 of 1983 deals with this.

What workers can do

  1. Follow the grazing plan. Move animals to the next camp on the day you are told. Let rested camps grow back.
  2. Count the animals. Too many animals for the veld causes overgrazing. Report if numbers grow.
  3. Check water every day. Fix or report leaks and dirty troughs.
  4. Watch the animals. Report animals that are thin, panting a lot, shivering or sick.
  5. Look after shelter. Keep shade and windbreaks in good condition.
  6. Stop erosion early. Report new gullies and bare patches. Help to pack branches or stones in small gullies if asked.
  7. Look after waste. Put containers and plastic in the right place.

Seasons and planning

SeasonWhat to watch
SummerHeat, ticks, flies, storms and erosion
AutumnSave grass for winter
WinterCold, dry grass, licks, fire risk
SpringBirths, first green grass, do not graze too early

Fire

Dry winter veld burns easily. A fire can kill animals and destroy grazing. Do not make fires in the veld. If you see a fire, warn others and tell your supervisor at once. Do not try to fight a big fire alone.

Key points

  • Weather, grass, water and shelter all affect animal health and growth.
  • Too many animals in one camp for too long causes overgrazing and erosion.
  • Keep kraals and manure away from rivers and dams.
  • Follow the grazing plan and check water every day.
  • Report thin or sick animals, new gullies and fires straight away.
